recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Preserve Duration/Range/Period as the base Timing.repeat.bounds[x] choices and use later extension-path decisions when explicit start-date plus duration/range modeling is required.
issue_request: FHIR-8344 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification FHIR-core datatypes change request asking to support Timing.repeat.bounds as a Quantity for medication schedules such as TID for 14 days without knowing an outpatient start date. The issue was resolved as done under another task, with a comment noting that Timing.repeat.bounds[x] already had a duration.
initial_application: No independent FHIR-8344-tagged source commit was found. The request was satisfied by the same Timing.repeat.bounds[x] history as FHIR-5951 and FHIR-6252: fca58ccc39dd07aaf03838155eb8654a5f713d9c converted Period-only bounds to bounds[x] with Duration support, and 2fbb4392eeaedcf258c8e4f38bbe77af755cb2d6 added Range to the same choice element.
additional_context: Timing is active and normative in source/fhir.ini. The authoritative Timing spreadsheet defines Timing.repeat.bounds[x] as Duration | Range | Period, Duration is a Quantity representing a length of time, and the datatypes examples page includes the seed's TID for 14 days pattern using boundsDuration. Later FHIR-31559 chose an extension route for explicit start-date plus Duration/Range modeling rather than changing the base bounds[x] choices.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. Adding a generic Quantity choice would be broader than the accepted modification because the current source already provides the time-valued Quantity semantics through Duration.
